_state_shape: The state is the raw chapter prose (design A) or one consecutive window of it (design B). No title, tense or book metadata is added: the decision is about the sentences.

breaks.instructions: At least one sentence in this passage fails to resolve to a single, clear, unambiguous meaning for a reader moving through it once, left to right, in order.

criteria.true: At least one sentence makes the meaning break. Examples of a break: a pro-verb or elliptical stand-in ('do', 'is', 'did', 'one') stands for a verb or phrase the sentence never supplies, so the reader cannot recover what is meant; the natural first parse of a sentence contradicts what it must mean, forcing a reread (garden path or mis-bracketing); a modifier attaches to the wrong noun; the two halves of an interrupted quotation, read as one sentence across the action beat, say something other than what the speaker means; a pronoun or definite phrase ('it', 'that', 'this', 'the guy') has no antecedent the reader can pin; the phrasing is logically inverted or self-contradicting; a second unintended reading (crude, comic, or literal) collides with the scene; a plainly wrong word is used for the intended meaning; a stated count or number contradicts what the passage itself shows.
criteria.false: Every sentence resolves to one meaning on a first straight-through read. Rough grammar in the service of voice is NOT a break and does not make this true: sentence fragments and one-word sentences used for pacing; run-on 'and ... and ... and' stacking and comma splices inside first-person narration or dialogue; sentences opening with And, But, So or Because; trailing, interrupted or repeated-for-rhythm sentences; compressed or elliptical phrasing whose meaning the reader still recovers inside the same sentence.

clean.instructions: How cleanly does this passage read on a single straight-through first pass, judged only on whether each sentence resolves to one meaning?
criteria: Several sentences break: a reader moving once through the passage lands on the wrong meaning or on no meaning more than twice, and has to stop and re-read to recover the sense.
One or two sentences break: a reader moving once through the passage lands on the wrong meaning or no meaning once or twice and has to re-read those sentences.
No sentence breaks, but one or more sentences are compressed or elliptical enough that the reader works briefly for the meaning before recovering it inside the same sentence.
Every sentence resolves to one meaning immediately on the first pass; nothing makes the reader work for the sense.

design_b.state: one consecutive window of the chapter, about 400-500 words, split on paragraph boundaries; windows cover the chapter with no overlap
design_b.chapter_score: max over the chapter's windows of P(breaks = true); the mean is recorded too

breaks.instructions: IDENTICAL to design_a.questions.breaks (same instructions and same criteria strings), so the only difference between the two designs is how much text the model sees at once.
